Spend and calls. 424 credits: four qwen-image-2.1 stills at 10 each (two references, each repainted once after a failed check) and two 8-second minimax-h3 480p text-to-video calls at 192 each. Two paid tools, six paid calls. The rest is free: vision yes/no checks, the text LLM (story, screenplay, two prompts) and ffmpeg (frames and the stitch).

The references. Clip 1 got @shop (the shop front with the lettered sign, second paint) and @bouquet (the finished product). Clip 2 got @previous (clip 1's last frame) and @shop again, reused at no cost because its sign must be spelled. Clip 2 did not get @bouquet: the vision model found it in @previous. No person reference was made for either clip; the florist and the customer were carried by the last frame.

What held across the cut. The place, the people, the light and the camera. Clip 2's first frame repeats clip 1's last frame almost exactly: the same green shop front and brass bell, the same open glazed door, Mara in her green apron inside on the left, and Eli in a pale-blue overshirt on the right. Their arms are also raised the same way. The SSIM between the two frames is 0.607. The vision model answered yes to same Mara, same Eli, and same place and light. The end of the film is right: the camera pulls back to the full shop front, the sign reads exactly “Petal & Stem”, Eli holds the bouquet and Mara stands in the doorway.

What broke: the bouquet. At about 6 s in clip 1, a hand from off-screen (neither Mara's nor Eli's) pushes the finished bouquet into the frame. From 7 s to the last frame the bouquet hangs in mid-air against the door glass while Mara's hands are empty. Clip 2 picks up that frame faithfully, floating bouquet included. It also gives Mara a second bouquet, so at 0–1 s there are two. The floating one is gone by about 2 s, and the handover from Mara to Eli then plays cleanly.

Why it got through. The last-frame check flagged it: “Mara holds the completed bouquet at chest height?” was answered no, with “bouquet is suspended separately”. But the state manager only acts when an element is missing from the last frame, not when it is in the wrong state. So it fed the broken frame forward. The fix: when a state question fails on the last frame, regenerate the clip, or send @previous from an earlier frame where the state is right together with the product reference.

Other faults. (1) Clip 1 ignored “one continuous shot, no cuts”. It opens on the empty shop front with the door already open (the unlocking is skipped), shows Mara at the counter, cuts to two close-ups of hands wrapping the flowers on cream paper (3.5–5 s), then cuts back outside. Eight seconds was too short for three beats, so the model cut. (2) The @bouquet repaint was wasted: the check demanded “a simple knot”, both paints tied a bow, and the clips kept the bow throughout. The check was more specific than the film needed. The @shop repaint was justified: the first sign read “Petal & Stem.” with a trailing period. (3) Sound: ambience and soft music, no speech asked for. The transcriber heard “Na máquina.” on clip 1; this could be two unasked Portuguese words or the transcriber inventing them on music, and it was not checked by ear.
